A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same survey, with matching core sections and accessible figures, tables, equations, and references. Neither contains an appendix. Added and relocated material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v2 presents literature summaries, taxonomies, and illustrative task examples. Empirical findings are attributed to cited studies; no original experiments or empirical data-analysis results are reported.

after.justification: v4 remains a literature survey. Its additional model descriptions, architecture entries, and benchmark summaries do not report original empirical results.

M1.justification: The SpeechLM definition and tokenizer–language model–vocoder framework are retained. Added descriptions of existing systems do not introduce or modify an algorithm proposed by this work.

E1.justification: Neither version conducts training or evaluation on datasets. Table VI adds VoxDialogue and changes VoiceBench's listed output modality from audio to text, but these revise the benchmark catalog rather than coverage actually evaluated by the survey.

E2.justification: Table II gains surveyed systems, but it compares architectural attributes rather than experimental performance against a proposed method. Neither version reports an evaluated baseline comparison.

E3.justification: Section VI-A revises VERT's description from k-grams that appear at least once to k-grams that repeat at least once. This changes the reported metric criterion, without establishing any implemented evaluation change or experimental rerun.

E4.justification: No ablations, robustness tests, error analyses, or empirical case studies are added or removed. The new turn-taking benchmark descriptions review evaluation resources rather than present analyses performed by this work.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests for this work. Descriptions of cited studies' sampling and statistical evaluation measures are retained.

E6.justification: The added table entries describe architectures and benchmark metadata, not empirical outcomes. Existing literature-derived performance findings are retained, and no numerical performance results or new empirical findings are introduced.

T1.justification: Section III-A adds HuBERT's masked objective and iterative target-update rule (Equations 2–3), plus EnCodec's residual-quantization formulation (Equation 4), beyond v2's generic tokenizer equations. The original SpeechLM and GAN-loss mathematics remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution claims, and conclusion retain the same scope: a comprehensive SpeechLM survey covering components, training, applications, evaluation, and challenges. The claimed first-survey contribution is unchanged.

C2.justification: Section IV-C distinguishes basic streaming interaction from full-duplex communication and explains why streaming alone cannot capture more sophisticated conversational behavior. v2 characterized real-time interaction primarily through interruption and simultaneous response. Section VII's challenges remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v4 adds technical descriptions such as HuBERT's MFCC-based initial clustering and HiFi-GAN's generator-only inference. Table II revises Zeng et al.'s tokenizer from Whisper + ASR to Whisper + VQ. These are documentation changes; the survey repository link is retained.

R1.justification: The literature coverage substantially expands through a new Connections with other surveys paragraph, architectural entries including Kimi-Audio, Qwen2.5-Omni, Minmo, and USDM, and benchmarks including VoxDialogue, Full Duplex Bench, and Talking Turns. This broadens the survey's research coverage beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: v4 adds representative-component explanations, rewrites and renames Section IV-C from Speech Generation Paradigm to Speech Interaction Paradigm, and removes a duplicated Interactive Period Recognition paragraph. The overall section structure and most prose are retained.

P2.justification: v4 adds Figure 3 illustrating semantic, acoustic, and mixed tokenizers. The previous taxonomy becomes Figure 4 with updated entries, and Tables II and VI gain rows. Existing display structures and the two-column layout are largely retained.

improvement.justification: The tokenizer illustration and component explanations improve accessibility, while the streaming/full-duplex distinction, removal of duplicated prose, and revised VERT description improve clarity. Expanded literature coverage makes the survey more useful. These gains outweigh the limited traceability defect introduced by the unresolved ICoT [?] citation in Table II, while the central synthesis remains largely unchanged.
